A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gumbel-based counterfactual generation work. Their text, equations, algorithms, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, similarity measurements, gender-steering outcomes, and knowledge-editing results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 reports original edit-distance distributions, knowledge-editing outcomes, and generated counterfactual examples in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Proposition 3.1 change the stated posterior sampler: v1 draws the observed token's noise from a standard Gumbel; v3 samples the perturbed maximum using the log-sum-exp location, samples truncated competitors, and subtracts logits to recover noise. Generation also changes from a fixed token count to stopping at EOS, with fresh noise beyond the observed length. These alter the procedure, independently of the formalism's renaming.

E1.justification: Wikipedia and Bios remain represented, including retained GPT2-XL gender examples in Appendix E.2. v3 adds targeted koala-habitat prompts and counterfactuals in Section 4.2/Figure 5; v1 evaluated the koala edit only on neutral Wikipedia prompts.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same six intervention conditions: GPT2-XL gender steering and two MEMIT edits, plus LLaMA3 gender steering, Honest steering, and instruction tuning. Neither version evaluates an alternative counterfactual generator against the proposed procedure. v3's inverse-CDF comparison is attributed to cited work.

E3.justification: The principal evaluation replaces normalized longest-common-prefix length and E5 cosine similarity with normalized character edit distance. Appendix D.2 expands the reported Louvre prompt list from eight to thirteen while retaining 75 filtered sentences. The Wikipedia protocol retains 500 sentences, five-word prompts, and a maximum 25-token original continuation.

E4.justification: v1's 500-biography LLaMA3 gender study, including pronoun outcomes and word-probability-ratio analysis, is removed rather than relocated. Its LLaMA3 appendix examples also disappear, although GPT2-XL Bios examples remain. v3 expands the targeted knowledge-editing case studies with Louvre and koala examples in Figures 4–5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both show distributions across generated sentences; the changed histograms do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v3 replaces the prefix-length and cosine-similarity results with edit-distance results and removes the quantitative gender outcomes and word rankings. Louvre outcomes change from 60.0% Rome/40.0% Paris to 54.6%/45.4%. The expanded prompt list and revised stated sampler prevent treating this as a same-setting performance decline. New MEMIT examples and changed GPT2-XL steering outputs also alter the reported qualitative evidence.

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces the general GSEM formulation with explicit acyclic and well-founded SEM definitions, ordering assumptions, and an LM construction. New Appendix B discusses identifiability and states a Thurstone/Gumbel characterization theorem. Proposition 3.1 is substantively revised, and Appendix C.2 supplies a detailed posterior-sampling derivation in place of v1's brief argument.

C1.justification: The central claims about generating conditional counterfactuals and exposing intervention side effects remain. v3's introduction adds an explicit qualification that the Gumbel causal parameterization is not unique and motivates its selection through the Thurstone model, refining the scope of the contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses non-identifiability, dependence on the chosen causal mechanism, counterfactual stability, and alternative sampling mechanisms. Its Louvre discussion changes from substantial semantic deviation to generally similar but nonminimal counterfactuals. Revised instruction-tuning examples acknowledge factual corrections and alternative correct facts, while the gender-stereotype mechanism discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v3 removes the project repository link advertised below v1's abstract; this establishes loss of an access pointer, not repository unavailability. Appendix D.2 supplies five additional explicit Louvre prompts. Appendix D.1 retains the intervention hyperparameters, model-access references, eight RTX-4096 GPUs, and 32-bit precision.

R1.justification: Appendix A replaces its earlier assertion that this formulation had not been explored in language modeling with a substantial comparison to concurrent Chatzi et al. work, distinguishing intervention scope and inference for observed sentences. The introduction and Appendix B substantially expand positioning through choice theory, Thurstone models, and alternative counterfactual mechanisms.

P1.justification: Sections 2–3 receive extensive rewriting around ASEM/WSEM terminology and a reorganized mathematical exposition. Section 4.2 loses its separate gender and Louvre subsections and becomes a MEMIT-focused discussion. Appendices B/C are reorganized into identifiability and proofs, and the title adds 'Gumbel.'

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn from two causal diagrams into a single language-process diagram. Figure 2 changes axes, legend ordering, and plotted distributions. The gender example figure is removed, two MEMIT example figures are introduced, and Figure 3 is reformatted with smaller text and without the earlier colored difference highlighting. Algorithm 1 is also reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects an important defect in the stated posterior sampler: the observed token's unconditional Gumbel draw is replaced by the conditional maximum construction, supported by Appendix C.2's derivation. The explicit identifiability discussion also substantially improves the interpretation of the central contribution. These gains outweigh the loss of the quantitative gender analysis, semantic-similarity measurements, and project link. The improvement concerns the documented method and reasoning; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were recomputed.
